_comment: NOOD_0201 — a real-shaped JIRA issue payload (Atlassian Document Format, spec-link boilerplate, ACs as loose Given/When/Then paragraphs). This is the 'ambiguous payload, little to no context' input: it names no base URL, and its ACs say POST /api/review — while the app actually serves POST /api/reviews/new. `noodle ticket` reads it, `noodle api-scan` supplies the missing URL, and the endpoint matcher corrects the route instead of authoring a 404.

fields.summary: Customer reviews: submit a review and list them newest-first

content.text: As a renter, I want to leave a review for BusterBlock and see the reviews other customers left, so the storefront shows real feedback.

fields.summary: Project Properties Values Project Name BusterBlock Project Description A VHS rental sample application Project Key BB

content.text: Given the reviews module is scaffolded in the target repository
Then it follows the provided Node and Express standards and includes baseline backend testing/tooling
Given a client submits POST /api/review with a valid JSON body containing a name value
Then the API validates the input, persists the review, and returns a JSON response containing id, name, date, and response
Given a client submits POST /api/review with missing, empty, or malformed JSON input
When the request reaches the API boundary
Then the API rejects the request with a client error response and does not persist a review record
Given a review is successfully submitted
Then exactly one record is stored with a generated UUID id, the submitted name, a timestamp, and the generated response text
When a client calls GET /api/reviews with pagination parameters
Then the API returns a paginated JSON list of reviews ordered by date descending
